definition: Attenuate means to reduce something in force or intensity; to weaken it.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word attenuate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know attenuate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: A double row of poplars planted along the fence line attenuates the prairie wind before it reaches the orchard.
Dampen is milder than attenuate — dampening a vibration takes the edge off it, while attenuating a signal can cut it to a small fraction of its strength.
Extinguish is stronger than attenuate — an attenuated beam still gets through, weakened, but an extinguished one is gone entirely.

Weaken is the plain, everyday word for making something less strong, and it claims nothing about how the loss happens. Attenuate is its technical relative: something attenuates a force by degrees, usually as the force passes through a barrier or medium, the way seawater attenuates sunlight.

Dilute means to weaken something by mixing another substance into it, as water thins juice or a long meeting dilutes enthusiasm. To attenuate is to cut strength as something passes through a barrier; to dilute is to thin it by adding to the mixture itself.

Muffle means to deaden sound specifically, usually by wrapping or covering the source — a scarf muffles a voice. Attenuate reaches far wider: signals, light, doses, and vibrations can all be attenuated, and the weakening is measured, not just hushed.

Attenuate means to reduce something in force or intensity; to weaken it.
Divers carry lamps below thirty meters because seawater attenuates sunlight, filtering out the reds first and dimming the rest, until the brightest noon above becomes a blue-gray dusk.
Attenuate is the precise choice when something is deliberately or physically weakened as it passes through a barrier or medium.
Unlike abate, which describes a force easing on its own, attenuate almost always has an agent — something does the weakening.
Attenuate belongs to physics, medicine, and engineering — signals, beams, doses, and vibrations are attenuated.
In everyday speech, 'weaken' or 'dampen' is the natural choice; reach for attenuate when something passes through a barrier or medium and comes out the other side reduced.
Compare abate, which is what a storm does on its own.

The first vaccines against the virus used a live but crippled strain.
Researchers grew the pathogen for hundreds of generations in cells it was poorly suited to, and each cycle attenuated it a little further.
By the fortieth generation the virus could still teach the immune system its shape, but its power to cause disease had fallen to a measured fraction of the original.
None of it was accident: technicians tracked the decline batch by batch, culling any strain that stayed too strong.
What reached the clinic was the same virus in outline only — present, recognizable, and too feeble to do harm.
